title: [com.gradleup.shadow:com.gradleup.shadow.gradle.plugin] Gradle Shadow: Zip Slip path traversal in ShadowCopyAction — no independent entry-name sanitization
summary:
Summary

ShadowCopyAction in the Shadow plugin does not validate or sanitize ZIP entry names before writing them to the output fat JAR. A malicious upstream dependency containing path traversal sequences (e.g. ../../../../tmp/pwned.txt) in entry names will have those entries reproduced verbatim in the output shadow JAR.

Details

The vulnerability exists because Shadow relies entirely on Gradle's ZipFileTree for entry sanitization rather than implementing its own path validation. This means:

  1. Users on Gradle < 7.6.2 / 8.x < 8.2.0 are directly exploitable
  2. The produced shadow JAR becomes a Zip Slip weapon against any downstream consumer using unprotected extraction (raw ZipInputStream, older CI tooli
summary_ko: [com.gradleup.shadow:com.gradleup.shadow.gradle.pl

title: [org.json:json] JSON-java: JSONTokener Has Unbounded Numeric String Resource-Exhaustion DoS
summary:
1. Executive Summary

JSON-java version 20260522 contains an unguarded path from an HTTP request body to unbounded BigInteger and BigDecimal construction. JSONTokener.nextSimpleValue() accumulates numeric characters into a StringBuilder with no length cap, then passes the full string to JSONObject.stringToNumber(), which calls new BigInteger(val) or new BigDecimal(val) directly. Both constructors have polynomial time complexity (O(n^1.585) for BigInteger).

title: [org.zeroturnaround:zt-zip] zt-zip: ZipUtil.unpack can change file permissions of output directory
summary:
Summary

When using one of the ZipUtil.unpack overloads, the file permissions of the output directory can be changed. For example, when the output directory was only accessible to the 'owner' it could be instead made accessible to every OS user.

Details

When the name of a ZIP entry resolves to the output directory itself (e.g. the name /), the path traversal checks permit it and then perform actions on that directory, such as applying the file permissions of the ZIP entry to it.

PoC

This proof of concept requires an OS with support for POSIX file permissions. This issue itself is however not limited to those OS' with POSIX file permissions, see zt-zip's ZTFilePermissionsUtil.fetchD
summary_ko: [org.zeroturnaround:zt-zip] zt-zip: ZipUtil.unpack

title: [org.zeroturnaround:zt-zip] zt-zip: Path traversal in fluent API unpack
summary:
Summary

ZipUtil.unpack(...) rejects ZIP entries that escape the target output directory, but the Zips fluent API appears to use a separate unpack implementation that does not apply the same destination-boundary check.

A ZIP entry such as:

../escape/poc.txt

is written outside the configured destination directory when processed with:

Zips.get(zip).unpack().destination(outputDir).process();

The transformer branch is affected as well.
